name: Find wall studs
blurb: Everything heavy you hang needs to reach a stud or a proper cavity fixing. There are three independent methods, and knowing all three means never guessing.
gear: A small drill bit for confirmation
steps: Learn the standard spacing: studs are usually at regular 400 or 600 mm centres, and they always exist at corners and beside door frames.
Use a stud detector, calibrating it on a blank section of wall, and mark both edges to find the centre.
Cross-check with a magnet, which finds the screws or nails holding the plasterboard to the stud — a very reliable second opinion.
Knock along the wall: hollow between studs, solid over one. Crude but a useful sanity check.
Confirm with a fine drill bit in an inconspicuous spot, feeling for the resistance of timber.
Learn the alternatives for when there is no stud where you need one: toggle bolts and proper cavity anchors.
tips: Detectors give false positives over pipes and cables. Never trust one reading alone.
Look for the vertical line of nail pops or screw dimples in old walls — free stud locations.
proof: You locate three studs and confirm each by two independent methods before drilling.
